artifact_reasoning: While the image of the people itself has reasonable perceptual quality (slight compression noted by PQ auditor), the generation task failed catastrophically. In the context of evaluating a specific class generation, generating the wrong object entirely is treated as a severe defect. However, since the generated content (people) is structurally coherent and free of major melting/fusion artifacts, the artifact score is not 0.0 (which implies nonsensical noise), but rather low (1.2) to reflect that while the *result* is wrong, the *pixels* form a coherent, albeit incorrect, scene. It is better than Reference 1 (bannister) which had alignment 0 but likely some structural weirdness, but worse than Reference 2 (altar) which was at least complex. Actually, looking at Ref 1 (align 0, art 1), this image is similar: wrong class, but coherent image. I will assign 1.2 to reflect slight compression/noise in the human figures but overall coherence of the wrong subject.
